items.a: It depends on your list size and team size, not just the sticker price. Klaviyo's Email plan costs $20 a month at 500 active profiles; Mailchimp's Essentials plan starts at $13 a month for up to 500 contacts, and Mailchimp stays cheaper at solo-operator scale, $26.50 a month against Klaviyo's $30 at around 1,000 contacts. The gap can flip once a team gets involved: Klaviyo charges nothing extra for more people on one account, while Mailchimp's Essentials plan caps out at 3 seats and Standard at 5, so a five-person team can be forced onto a pricier Mailchimp plan at a contact count that wouldn't otherwise need it. At 50,000 contacts, Klaviyo runs $860 a month and Mailchimp runs $815, with Klaviyo's number driven up by email-send volume and Mailchimp's by seats, not list size, in both cases.

items.q: Which is better for a Shopify or WooCommerce store, Klaviyo or Mailchimp?
items.a: Klaviyo, for most stores with real order volume. It's built around Shopify and WooCommerce order and browsing history, so its email and SMS flows can target based on what a customer actually bought or viewed, and its Reviews add-on, $25 a month for up to 250 orders, is scoped specifically to that order data. Mailchimp isn't a bad fit either: purchase-behavior tracking and personalized product recommendations are included on every Mailchimp plan, even the free one, so a very small store can get basic ecommerce personalization at no cost before Klaviyo's paid tiers make sense. But Mailchimp has no add-on comparable to Klaviyo's Reviews, and its SMS marketing has no published flat rate, unlike Klaviyo's $0.01-per-segment published rate. Once a store has enough order volume to justify a dedicated ecommerce email platform, Klaviyo's tools are built for exactly that job in a way Mailchimp's more general feature set isn't.

items.q: Does Klaviyo or Mailchimp have a better free plan?
items.a: Both cap their free plans at 250 contacts and 500 email sends a month, which makes them closer than most comparisons suggest. Klaviyo's free plan adds a small monthly allowance of Composer AI and mobile-messaging usage at no extra charge, and includes full email support for the first 60 days after signup. Mailchimp's free plan also limits sends to 250 a day within that monthly cap, includes only 1 seat and 1 audience, has no automation flows or AI features at all, and its email support window is shorter, 30 days rather than 60. Neither plan raises its contact cap over time, and both are free indefinitely rather than time-limited, so the real choice on the free tier comes down to whether you want Klaviyo's AI and SMS allowance or Mailchimp's broader base feature set, such as landing pages and forms, at the same $0 price.

items.q: Do Klaviyo and Mailchimp offer a free trial?
items.a: Not in the same way. Klaviyo doesn't run a time-limited trial of a paid plan at all; instead it offers a free-forever plan capped at 250 active profiles, so you can use the real product indefinitely before ever paying. Mailchimp offers a genuine 14-day self-serve trial, but only on its Essentials and Standard plans, and only if you provide valid payment information at signup; the account is billed automatically the moment the trial ends unless you cancel first. Mailchimp's Premium plan skips that self-serve trial and instead offers a separate one-month trial arranged through its sales team, for qualified new customers only, not something you can start yourself. If you want to try before committing a card, Mailchimp's Essentials or Standard trial is the more literal free trial; if you'd rather use a real account indefinitely at no cost and upgrade only when you outgrow it, Klaviyo's free plan does that instead.

items.q: Does Klaviyo or Mailchimp charge extra for team members?
items.a: Mailchimp does, indirectly; Klaviyo doesn't. Klaviyo's Email plan is priced only by active-profile count, and nothing in its published pricing caps or charges for how many people log into one account. Mailchimp instead caps seats by plan: 3 on Essentials, 5 on Standard, and only Premium removes the limit entirely. That means a growing team can be forced to upgrade Mailchimp plans purely because it added a person, even if its contact list hasn't grown at all, while the same team on Klaviyo pays the same price it would with one person on the account. The trade-off is that Mailchimp's higher tiers add real capability alongside the extra seats, such as more automation-flow steps and, on Premium, phone support and a dedicated onboarding specialist, so an upgrade forced by headcount usually comes with more of the product too, not just a seat tax.

items.q: Can I send SMS marketing from Klaviyo or Mailchimp?
items.a: Yes from both, but only Klaviyo publishes what it costs. Klaviyo builds SMS in as a native, usage-priced channel: outbound texts to a US recipient from a toll-free number cost $0.01 per segment, with carrier fees already included in that rate, on top of whatever Email plan you're on. Mailchimp treats SMS and MMS as a separate add-on that isn't priced as a flat rate anywhere on its pricing or comparison pages; its help center says the per-message cost varies by the country you're sending to, and using it at all requires an application and approval process plus a separate monthly credit purchase, not a simple plan upgrade. If knowing your SMS cost in advance matters, Klaviyo's published per-segment rate is the more predictable option; Mailchimp's SMS is usable, but its actual dollar cost isn't something you can check on the public pricing page before signing up.

items.q: What happens if I go over my plan's limit on Klaviyo or Mailchimp?
items.a: Differently, and neither outcome is clearly better. On Klaviyo, exceeding your Email plan's active-profile tier triggers 'profile compliance': you're automatically moved to a pricier, profile-compliant tier at the start of your next billing cycle, whether or not you opted into any upgrade preference; the only way to avoid it is suppressing enough profiles at least 24 hours before renewal. For email-send overages specifically, Klaviyo lets you choose a one-time flexible charge, a permanent auto-upgrade, or pausing sends instead. Mailchimp's pricing and comparison pages both carry a footnote that overage charges apply once you exceed your contact or send limit, but neither page states what that overage actually costs per contact or per email. You can know Klaviyo's mechanism and price it in advance; Mailchimp's overage exists, but its exact dollar cost isn't published anywhere a prospective customer can check before signing up.
